Sure. Before any rendering even starts, Claude — acting as a Design Director — reads your style fingerprint and room context and produces a structured design brief: what the anchor piece is, the color palette, materials, lighting concept, object hierarchy. Then a second Claude call compresses that into a tight 50-to-80-word FLUX prompt with your LoRA trigger words baked in.

Then it hits Modal and runs four passes. Pass zero is a Claude vision layout planner that looks at the empty room and decides what goes where spatially. Pass one is the hero lock — FLUX general image-to-image at high strength, around 0.92, with your full LoRA stack loaded: the style LoRA, a detail enhancer, and a realism LoRA. This is the main creative hit that establishes the whole look. Pass two comes in at much lower strength, around 0.55, and adds per-surface decor — textiles, smaller objects, surface details. Pass three is a relighting pass using IC-Light, which harmonizes the scene's lighting so it feels coherent; if that fails it just falls back to pass two's result.

After all that, there's an in-process editorial step — warm color balance, an S-curve, a touch of grain and vignette — and then Claude runs a ten-axis quality score on the final render and spits out three suggested refinement chips for the user.
